title: Foundations: Stadium Rock - The Complete Guide
summary: What Stadium Rock is, where it came from, and how its songs work.
body:
Stadium Rock songs: Rock anthems are built to be shouted by thousands: huge choruses, power chords, and a beat that unites the arena. The formula is verse, bigger verse, then a chorus the crowd sings for you.

History: The Who's 1970s arena shows, Queen's We Will Rock You (1977), and Journey's Don't Stop Believin' (1981) wrote the playbook. Springsteen, U2, and Foo Fighters keep the form alive.

How the songs work: Stadium Rock favors the keys of E, A, G, D. Common forms include Verse–pre-chorus–chorus, guitar solo, final double chorus; Build from quiet verse to explosive chorus. Players should master power chords: root+fifth, no third first, then the pre-chorus lift: drums build, chords rise. Power-chord keys; capo rarely needed.

title: Don't Stop Believin' - Stadium Rock Song Study

body:
